chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali Al-Neysabouri, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a Muslim who became a Christian. He said: 'He is killed and is not asked to repent.' I said, 'So if a Christian became a Muslim, then reneged from Islam?' He said: 'He is asked to repent; if he returns (to Islam), fine, otherwise he is killed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in legal ruling for apostasy between a Muslim becoming Christian and a Christian becoming Muslim then leaving Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a key jurisprudential distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the penalty for apostasy (hadd al-murtadd), differentiating between the 'fitri' apostate (a Muslim by birth or default) and the 'hanifi' or convert apostate. For the former, Imam al-Reza (AS) rules immediate execution without waiting for repentance (la yustatab), reflecting the view that their departure is a fundamental breach of innate faith. Conversely, for a non-Muslim who embraced Islam and then left, the individual is given a period to repent (yustatab), aligning with the principle of giving new converts time to solidify their commitment before facing the hadd penalty.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali Al Neysabouri, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a Muslim who became a Christian. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be killed, and would not be told to repent’. I said, ‘So if a Christian became a Muslim, then reneged from Al-Islam?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be told to repent, so if he were to return (fine) or else killed’.
